    - heading [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Amazon Route 53 provides highly available and scalable
      - link "Domain Name System (DNS)":
        - /url: /route53/what-is-dns/
      - text: ","
      - link "domain name registration":
        - /url: /blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/benefits-of-domain-registration-with-amazon-route-53/
      - text: ", and"
      - link "health-checking":
        - /url: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover.html
      - text: cloud services. It is designed to give developers and businesses an extremely reliable and cost-effective way to route end users to internet applications by translating names like example.com into the numeric IP addresses, such as 192.0.2.1, that computers use to connect to each other. You can combine your Route 53 DNS with health-checking services to route traffic to healthy endpoints or to independently monitor and alarm on endpoints. You can also use the
      - link "Traffic Flow":
        - /url: /route53/traffic-flow/
      - text: visual policy builder to simplify the implementation of your routing policies, and you can purchase and manage domain names such as example.com and automatically configure DNS settings for your domains. In addition,
      - link "Route 53 Resolver":
        - /url: /route53/resolver/
      - text: provides a regional DNS service that performs recursive DNS lookups for names hosted in Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2), as well as public names on the internet. Lastly, the
      - link "Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall":
        - /url: /route53/resolver-dns-firewall/
      - text: allows you to block queries made for known or suspected malicious domains, and to allow queries for trusted domains when using the Route 53 Resolver for recursive DNS resolution.

limitations: Event sequence records provider receipt order; simultaneous browser causality is not inferred.
Network content is retained only when selected; Playwright response-body bytes are API results and are not guaranteed to match wire bytes.
Request bytes are limited to what Playwright exposes; not_exposed does not establish body absence or multipart file coverage.
Network content reads settle within 5 seconds each and the observer does not request bodies from unfinished responses.
Playwright scenario events do not expose request initiator stacks; receipt order does not prove causality.
Storage values are hashed only after declared-secret redaction.
